info.title: x.md API
info.summary: Read public X posts, threads, profiles, connections and search results as Markdown or JSON.
info.description:
x.md is a read-only HTTP API over public X (Twitter) content. Every operation is a `GET`, none of them needs credentials, and each returns compact Markdown by default, expanded Markdown with `full=true`, or structured JSON with `format=json` or `Accept: application/json`.

x.md never posts, replies, follows, likes or writes anything to X, and it cannot read protected or deleted content.

Use it when an agent needs the text of a post, a thread, a profile, a follower list or a search result in a form it can parse, without running a browser or holding X credentials.

Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents (`application/problem+json`, or `application/json` when the request asks for it) carrying a stable machine `code`, a human `detail`, a `resolution` telling the caller what to do next, and a `documentation_url`.

Pagination is cursor-first: list responses return an opaque `nextCursor`; send it back as `cursor` with the same query and options. An ordinal `page` (1-10) exists as a fallback and is slower. `limit` defaults to 20 and is capped at 100.

Quotas are advertised on every response with the IETF `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` structured fields, plus the `RateLimit-Limit` / `RateLimit-Remaining` / `RateLimit-Reset` compatibility triple; a 429 also carries `Retry-After`. Cached reads do not consume the live-lookup quota.

Versioning and deprecation.

The stable machine surface is `/api/v1/*`, and `v1` is the current major version. Additive changes — new optional query parameters, new response fields — ship inside `v1` without a version bump, so ignore response fields you do not recognise. Breaking changes ship under a new path prefix (`/api/v2/*`), and `/api/v1/*` keeps working for at least 12 months after its successor is published.

The permalink routes (`/{handle}`, `/{handle}/status/{id}`, `/{handle}/followers`, `/{handle}/following`, `/search`, `/oembed`) are the unversioned product surface. They mirror x.com URLs, they are stable, and they are not deprecated.

Scheduled for deprecation on 2026-09-15: `GET /api/convert` (successor `GET /api/v1/posts`) and `GET /api/browse`, whose successor depends on its `resource` (`resource=profile` → `/api/v1/profiles/{handle}`, `resource=followers` → `/api/v1/profiles/{handle}/followers`, `resource=following` → `/api/v1/profiles/{handle}/following`, `resource=search` → `/api/v1/search`). Both aliases keep working unchanged until the sunset date, and they announce the schedule now, ahead of the date the `Deprecation` field names: every response from them carries `Deprecation: @1789430400` (RFC 9745, an `@`-prefixed Unix timestamp for 2026-09-15T00:00:00Z), `Sunset: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 00:00:00 GMT` (RFC 8594, an HTTP-date, never earlier than the deprecation date), and a `Link` header carrying `rel="deprecation"` and `rel="sunset"`. `rel="successor-version"` joins them whenever the request names a route that replaces it, which for `/api/browse` means a `resource` that resolves; a browse call that names none is answered without it. Read `Deprecation` and `Sunset` on every response, follow `rel="successor-version"` when it is present, and stop calling the alias before the sunset date.

Written policy: https://x.pcstyle.dev/docs/versioning. Machine description: https://x.pcstyle.dev/openapi.json.

x-error-catalog.note: A 502 or 503 may also carry a provider-specific code such as `fxtwitter_error`, `contextdev_empty`, `firecrawl_network` or `all_providers_failed`. Those share the resolution of `upstream_error`.

missing_url.title: Missing url parameter
missing_url.resolution: Add `?url=<public X status URL>`, or call `/{handle}/status/{id}` directly.

invalid_url.title: Invalid X status URL
invalid_url.resolution: Pass a public x.com or twitter.com status URL in `url`, for example `?url=https://x.com/jack/status/20`.

unsupported_host.title: Unsupported host
unsupported_host.resolution: Only x.com and twitter.com status URLs are supported. Rewrite the host and retry.

invalid_path.title: Not a status permalink
invalid_path.resolution: Use a permalink shaped like https://x.com/{handle}/status/{id}.

invalid_params.title: Invalid handle or status id
invalid_params.resolution: Provide `handle` (1-15 word characters) and a numeric `id`.

invalid_option.title: Invalid query option
invalid_option.resolution: Fix the parameter named in `detail`. Dates are ISO dates, ISO datetimes, or unix timestamps; `since` must be earlier than `until`; counts are positive integers within the documented maximum.

invalid_handle.title: Invalid X handle
invalid_handle.resolution: Handles are 1-15 characters of letters, digits, or underscores, with no leading @.

invalid_format.title: Unsupported format
invalid_format.resolution: Use `format=markdown`, `format=obsidian`, or `format=json`. Browse accepts markdown or json.

invalid_thread.title: Invalid thread parameter
invalid_thread.resolution: Use `thread=off`, `full`, `conversation`, or a number from 2 to 100.

invalid_mode.title: Invalid mode parameter
invalid_mode.resolution: See the parameter tables at https://x.pcstyle.dev/docs/responses.

invalid_body.title: Invalid JSON body
invalid_body.resolution: Send a well-formed JSON object, or omit the body entirely.

invalid_key.title: Invalid or disabled API key
invalid_key.resolution: Remove the Authorization header to call anonymously, or present a valid `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

unauthorized.title: Unauthorized
unauthorized.resolution: This route is private. The public read-only API needs no credentials; see https://x.pcstyle.dev/openapi.json.

not_found.title: Not found
not_found.resolution: Confirm the post or profile is public and still exists on x.com, then retry. Deleted and protected content is never available.

route_not_found.title: API route not found
route_not_found.resolution: Discover the public API through https://x.pcstyle.dev/api, https://x.pcstyle.dev/openapi.json, or https://x.pcstyle.dev/.well-known/api-catalog.

method_not_allowed.title: Method not allowed
method_not_allowed.resolution: x.md is read-only. Use GET, HEAD, or OPTIONS; the `Allow` response header lists what this route accepts.

not_acceptable.title: No acceptable representation
not_acceptable.resolution: Request `text/markdown`, `application/json`, or `text/html`, or omit the Accept header.

rate_limited.title: Rate limit exceeded
rate_limited.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header, then retry. Cached responses do not count against the allowance.

internal_error.title: Unexpected error
internal_error.resolution: Retry with exponential backoff. If it persists, open an issue at https://github.com/pc-style/x-md/issues.

upstream_error.title: Upstream provider error
upstream_error.resolution: Retry with backoff. x.md reads a third-party provider that can fail independently.

upstream_rate_limited.title: Upstream provider is rate limiting x.md
upstream_rate_limited.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then retry. Bulk imports back off per page automatically; lower `concurrency` if this repeats.

search_unavailable.title: Search temporarily unavailable
search_unavailable.resolution: Wait the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then retry. Photos, Videos, and Users need configured sessions.

admin_unconfigured.title: Admin is not configured
admin_unconfigured.resolution: Set X_MD_ADMIN_TOKEN on the deployment. This route is not part of the public API.

x-pagination.exact_pages: Every page holds exactly `limit` items until the list ends; x.md assembles it from as many upstream pages as needed. A cursor may carry an offset (`…@15`); treat it as opaque.
x-pagination.termination: Stop when `nextCursor` is absent. A short or empty page is not the end of the list.
x-pagination.notes: Cursors are provider-tagged. Return one only to the same route, query and feed that issued it. Degraded search results carry no cursor. Own-account search feeds answer at most 20 per request.
x-pagination.bulk: For an account's whole history use `/{handle}/posts` (`since`, `until`, `max_posts`, `format=ndjson`) instead of paging.

get.summary: Read a post, thread or conversation
get.description:
Read one public X post as Markdown or JSON. Identify it either with `url` (a full status permalink) or with the `handle` and `id` pair.

A post is returned with whatever thread and conversation context the upstream provider exposes; use `thread` and `replies` to widen or narrow it. Send `Accept: application/json` (or `format=json`) for the structured body, `Accept: text/markdown` for Markdown. Markdown is the default when neither is given. Nothing is ever written back to X.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Public x.com or twitter.com status permalink. Required unless `handle` and `id` are supplied instead.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: X account handle without the leading `@`: 1-15 letters, digits or underscores. Reserved site paths (`/docs`, `/about`, `/search`, `/api`, ...) are never handles.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Numeric status id of the post. On the query surface it must be paired with `handle`, and is ignored when `url` is present.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Output representation. Overrides `Accept` negotiation. `obsidian` emits Obsidian-flavoured Markdown with wiki links.

parameters.name: thread
parameters.description: How much of the surrounding thread to include: `off` for the single post, `full` or `conversation` for everything available, or a post count from 2 to 100.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: `full` walks parents and replies around the post; `thread` keeps only the author's own chain.

parameters.name: replies
parameters.description: Which replies to include: the ranked `top` replies, the most `recent` ones, or `off`.

parameters.name: userinfo
parameters.description: Author metadata to render into the Markdown: `off`, the thread `author` only, or `all` participants.

parameters.name: full
parameters.description: Return the expanded representation: metrics, timestamps and profile counts instead of the compact default.

parameters.name: nocache
parameters.description: Bypass the application cache and fetch from the upstream provider. Charged against the live-lookup quota.

200.description: The post, its thread and the surrounding conversation. JSON carries the rendered Markdown alongside the structured posts.

get.summary: Read a profile and its latest posts
get.description:
Read a public X account: its bio, counts, and its most recent posts. Original posts only unless `with_replies` or `with_reposts` is set.

Results are paged: prefer the opaque `nextCursor` from the previous response over the ordinal `page`. Send `Accept: application/json` (or `format=json`) for the structured body, `Accept: text/markdown` for Markdown. Markdown is the default when neither is given.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: X account handle without the leading `@`: 1-15 letters, digits or underscores. Reserved site paths (`/docs`, `/about`, `/search`, `/api`, ...) are never handles.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from a previous response, and the preferred way to page: there is no limit on how far a cursor chain goes. Send it back with the same query, feed and options. Never decode a cursor, edit it, or reuse it across feeds. A cursor takes precedence over `page`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Ordinal page, used only when no `cursor` is supplied. Values above 10 are clamped. Numbered paging walks every preceding upstream page, so it is slower than a cursor.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum posts in the page. Values above 100 are clamped to 100. A page is assembled from as many upstream pages as it takes and cut exactly at `limit`; its `nextCursor` continues right after the last post.

parameters.name: with_replies
parameters.description: Include the account's replies. Off by default: the page then holds original posts only.

parameters.name: with_reposts
parameters.description: Include the account's reposts. Off by default. A repost is returned as the original post with `reposted_by` set, so it carries the original's `id` and `created_at`.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Start the page just below this instant instead of at the newest post. Lets a client jump straight to a date without walking cursors. Ignored when `cursor` is supplied.

get.summary: Import a profile's post history in bulk
get.description: Bulk history for onboarding and memory: the whole requested range in one request, as raw JSON that preserves every upstream field (`id`, `text`, `created_at`, `author`, `replying_to`, `quote`, `reposted_by`, `media`, `likes`, `replies`, `retweets`, `quotes`, `views`, `bookmarks`, `url`). x.md walks the timeline upstream in parallel instead of one cursor at a time, so a 2000-post history takes seconds rather than minutes. No Markdown representation: this route is JSON only. Metered separately from ordinary reads: 10 imports per 15 minutes per IP, 60 per API key (`import-ip` / `import-key` in `RateLimit-Policy`).

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: X account handle without the leading `@`: 1-15 letters, digits or underscores. Reserved site paths (`/docs`, `/about`, `/search`, `/api`, ...) are never handles.

parameters.name: since

schema.description: ISO date (`2026-01-01`), ISO datetime, or unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds.

parameters.description: Oldest post to include. Omit to go as far back as upstream allows (X serves roughly the 3200 most recent timeline entries; `meta.floor_reached` says when that floor was hit).

parameters.name: until

schema.description: ISO date (`2026-01-01`), ISO datetime, or unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds.

parameters.description: Newest post to include. Defaults to now. To continue past a truncated result, send its `meta.oldest` here.

parameters.name: max_posts
parameters.description: Most posts to return, newest first. Values above 5000 are clamped. `meta.truncated` is true when the range held more.

parameters.name: with_replies
parameters.description: Include the account's replies. On by default.

parameters.name: with_reposts
parameters.description: Include the account's reposts. On by default. A repost is the original post with `reposted_by` set.

parameters.name: only_replies
parameters.description: Return only the account's replies.

parameters.name: concurrency
parameters.description: Upstream timeline chains walked at once, up to 32 per configured upstream (a deployment with a pool of N upstreams accepts N × 32). Higher is faster until the upstream throttles; lower it if imports answer 503 `upstream_rate_limited`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `json` answers once with every post sorted newest first. `ndjson` streams one `{"post": …}` line per post as the parallel chains deliver them (unsorted), then a final `{"meta": …, "profile": …}` line, or `{"error": …}` if the walk failed.

200.description: Every matching post in the range, newest first, with the profile and a `meta` block describing the walk.

schema.description: With `format=ndjson`: one JSON object per line. `{"post": Post}` lines as posts arrive, then one `{"meta": ImportMeta, "profile": Author}` line, or `{"error": Problem}` when the walk failed part-way.

get.description:
Search public X posts across the `latest`, `top`, `photos` and `videos` feeds, or search accounts with `feed=users`. `since` and `until` bound the results by date; `limit` goes up to 100 on the `latest` and `top` feeds.

Results are paged: prefer the opaque `nextCursor` over the ordinal `page`, and send a cursor back only to the feed that issued it. When live X search is unavailable, x.md may answer with web-indexed snippets marked `degraded: true` and no cursor. Send `Accept: application/json` (or `format=json`) for the structured body, `Accept: text/markdown` for Markdown. Markdown is the default when neither is given.

parameters.name: q

get.description:
Deprecated compatibility alias for the `/api/v1/profiles/*` and `/api/v1/search` operations, selected by the `resource` query parameter. Responses carry the RFC 9745 `Deprecation` header, the RFC 8594 `Sunset` header, and a `Link` with `rel="successor-version"`. Scheduled for removal on 2027-09-15; move to the versioned routes before then.

There is no single successor: the replacement depends on `resource` (`resource=profile` → `/api/v1/profiles/{handle}`, `resource=followers` → `/api/v1/profiles/{handle}/followers`, `resource=following` → `/api/v1/profiles/{handle}/following`, `resource=search` → `/api/v1/search`), and `x-successor-version-map` publishes the same mapping. A call that names no resolvable resource still carries `Deprecation` and `Sunset`, but no `successor-version` link.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Which browse resource to read. Each value has a dedicated `/api/v1` route that should be used instead.

parameters.description: X account handle without the leading `@`: 1-15 letters, digits or underscores. Reserved site paths (`/docs`, `/about`, `/search`, `/api`, ...) are never handles.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search terms. X search operators such as `from:`, `since:` and `filter:` are passed through. Required when `resource=search`.

parameters.name: feed
parameters.description: Which search feed to read. `media` is an alias for `photos`. Unrecognised values fall back to `latest`. `photos`, `videos` and `users` need a configured live provider and answer 503 when none is available.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from a previous response, and the preferred way to page: there is no limit on how far a cursor chain goes. Send it back with the same query, feed and options. Never decode a cursor, edit it, or reuse it across feeds. A cursor takes precedence over `page`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Ordinal page, used only when no `cursor` is supplied. Values above 10 are clamped. Numbered paging walks every preceding upstream page, so it is slower than a cursor.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum results in the page. Values above 100 are clamped to 100. A page is assembled from as many upstream pages as it takes and cut exactly at `limit`; when the cut falls inside an upstream page the `nextCursor` carries an offset (`…@15`), so nothing is lost or repeated. Searches served by own accounts (`photos`, `videos`, `users`, or a fallback) answer at most 20 per request and report that in `limit`.
